children.translated_text: The fourth
<s>Rasāyanakhaṇḍa</s> (Section on Rejuvenation).

body.translated_text: Of the <s>Rasaratnākara</s> (Ocean of Jewels of Mercury) composed by <s>Śrī Nityanātha Siddha</s>,

children.translated_text: First teaching.
Invocation of blessings.
Victorious is that king of mercury (<s>rasarāja</s>), the remover of the fear of death,
The treasury of all virtues, the authority on bodily rejuvenation (<s>kāyakalpa</s>);
When served, he destroys wrinkles and grey hair, increases virility,

children.text: sthiramapi kurute yaḥ kāmi nīnāṃ prasaṅgam || 1 ||
children.translated_text: And makes firm the company of passionate women. || 1 ||
Praise of bodily perfection (<s>dehasiddhi</s>).
Now I shall properly expound the most splendid bodily perfection (<s>dehasiddhi</s>),
Upon the attainment of which, all supernatural powers (<s>siddhis</s>) arise for human beings. || 2 ||
Without the body, nothing desirable exists in the three worlds;
Let effort be directed toward it. || 3 ||
Therefore, with every effort,
Preliminary procedures for the practice of <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation).
On an auspicious day under a favorable constellation (<s>nakṣatra</s>), having performed emesis and purgation,
Then, for special purification, the juice extracted from the <s>ketakī</s> (screwpine) plant — || 4 ||
One should drink it, as it removes the defect of salt.
One <s>kuḍava</s> (measure) each for three days,
<s>Viḍaṅga</s> (Embelia ribes), <s>vacā</s> (calamus), and <s>kuṣṭha</s> (costus), combined with <s>ketakī</s> juice — || 5 ||
Boiled and drunk for three days, this is supreme in removing the defect of acidity.
<s>Śyāmā</s>, <s>agni</s> (Plumbago), <s>viḍaṅga</s>, <s>tryūṣaṇa</s> (the three pungent spices), <s>triphalā</s> (the three fruits), <s>vṛṣa</s> (Adhatoda) — || 6 ||
<s>Saindhava</s> (rock salt), <s>devadāru</s> (cedar), and <s>mustā</s> (Cyperus) — all these in equal parts,
One <s>karṣa</s> (measure) to be licked with ghee; after seven days it destroys all defects (<s>doṣas</s>). || 7 ||
Thus, with the body purified, one should worship the deities and the <s>guru</s> (teacher),
In proper sequence, and then undertake the <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation). || 8 ||
The virgin (<s>kumārī</s>) and the <s>yoginī</s>,
Dietary regimen during mercury practice.
In a windless underground chamber, free from external worries,
With senses controlled and anger conquered, one should eat rice cooked in milk. || 9 ||
<s>Ṣaṣṭi</s> rice porridge, barley food, wheat, and <s>mudga</s> (mung bean) broth,
One may eat the meat of animals from dry lands (<s>jāṅgala</s>), or only milk. || 10 ||
Or one may eat <s>balā</s> (strengthening) food, avoiding greens and salt;

children.text: abhyaṅgaṃ mastunā kuryāt snānaṃ caiva sukhāmbunā || 11 ||
children.translated_text: One should anoint the body with buttermilk and bathe with warm water. || 11 ||
<s>Kākinī</s> woman, favorable to oneself and in the prime of youth, should be regularly enjoyed;
A

children.text: rasendre bhakṣyamāṇe tu kāmāndho jāyate naraḥ || 12 ||
children.translated_text: When mercury (<s>rasendra</s>) is being consumed, a man becomes blind with passion. || 12 ||

children.text: maithunena vinā tasya hyajīrṇo jāyate rasaḥ |
children.translated_text: Without sexual intercourse, the mercury becomes undigested in him;
Pain, hiccups, fainting, fever, and restlessness. || 13 ||
From indigestion arise trembling, burning,
Cough, dyspnea, loss of appetite, vomiting, dizziness, and delusion indeed arise;
Therefore, one should enjoy a beautiful woman and avoid an ugly one. || 14 ||
Things to be avoided during <s>rasāyana</s>.
Anointing with pungent oil, sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>), liquor, curd,

yasyāstu kuñcitāḥ keśāḥ śyāmā yā padmalocanā | surūpā
                                    taruṇaṃ bhinnavistīrṇajaghanasthalā || saṅkīrṇahṛdayā
                                    pīnastanabhāreṇa nāmitā | cumba nāliṅganasparśakomalā

children.translated_text: <s>Kaliṅga</s> (watermelon), <s>kāravallī</s> (bitter gourd), sour substances, oil, pumpkin (<s>kūṣmāṇḍa</s>), and mustard (<s>rājikā</s>) — || 15 ||
<s>Bilva</s> (wood apple), mushroom (<s>chatrāka</s>), <s>vārtāka</s> (eggplant), <s>vidala</s> (split grain), and <s>kākamācī</s> (black nightshade),

children.text: mūlakaṃ laśunaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ śītamuṣṇaṃ ca varjayet || 16 ||
children.translated_text: Radish, garlic, and pungent, cold, and hot substances — these should be avoided. || 16 ||

children.text: rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ tyājyaṃ divāsvāpaṃ ca maithunam |
children.translated_text: Night wakefulness, daytime sleeping, and sexual intercourse should be abandoned;
Quarrel, agitation, worry, and grief should also be avoided. || 17 ||
Treatment of adverse effects of <s>rasāyana</s>.
From improper administration arise colic, drowsiness, lethargy, fever, and restlessness;
For three days, to pacify these, one should drink the fruit of <s>karkaṭī</s> (cucumber) with water. || 18 ||
One should lick with citron (<s>mātuluṅga</s>) juice;
Or powder of <s>śuṇṭhī</s> (dry ginger) and <s>saindhava</s> (rock salt),
Or one should drink <s>sauvarcala</s> (black salt) with cow's urine to pacify that. || 19 ||
And <s>pātāla garuḍī</s>, with water —
<s>Vandhyā karkoṭakī</s> (a type of gourd), <s>puṅkhā</s>,
With <s>saindhava</s> (rock salt). || 20 ||
One should boil with eight times the quantity of water, reduce to one-eighth,
Drink it for three days — it destroys all disorders; this is spoken by <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: mūlaṃ vā kāravallyutthaṃ saindhavaṃ vā gavāṃ jalaiḥ || 21 ||
children.translated_text: Or the root of <s>kāravallī</s> (bitter gourd), or <s>saindhava</s> with cow's urine — || 21 ||
One <s>karṣa</s> measure for three days; it conquers all disorders.
This is stated for those who practice <s>rasāyana</s> but follow improper diet. || 22 ||
One should follow precisely this procedure in the practice of <s>rasāyana</s>;
When combined with proper method, it is nectar; without proper method, it is poison. || 23 ||
Assimilation of mercury (<s>rasasaṅkrāmaṇa</s>).
<s>Cāturjātaka</s> (four aromatics), camphor, and <s>kaṅkola</s> (cubeb), with <s>kaṭukī</s> (Picrorhiza) fruit —
One should chew with betel; this aids in the assimilation of mercury. || 24 ||
Method for calcination of mercury (<s>pāradamāraṇa</s>).
Now shall be properly expounded, first, the calcination of mercury (<s>pāradamāraṇa</s>),
Of mercury that has been given a 'face' (<s>samukha</s>) or whose impressions have been activated (<s>vāsanāmukhita</s>). || 25 ||
One should gradually calcine gold in equal proportion, as before; then,
Adding an equal amount of sulfur (<s>gandhaka</s>) to it, with juices of divine herbs — || 26 ||
One should grind in a mortar for three days; then seal it in a crucible (<s>mūṣā</s>);
Heat with cowdung fire for one day and night, or with husk fire for three nights. || 27 ||
Born of divine herbs;
The heated material should be ground again with seeds
In equal amount, grind in a mortar for four <s>yāmas</s> (watches); seal in a diamond crucible and blow. || 28 ||
It becomes calcined mercury (<s>bhasmasūta</s>) — that indeed is to be employed in all <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation formulas).
Second method of calcination of mercury.
And equal gold — grind with acids for one <s>yāma</s> (watch). || 29 ||
Pure mercury
Having washed, form a pellet; add half the pellet's weight of pure sulfur (<s>gandhaka</s>);
Add half the sulfur's weight of borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), and an amount of turmeric (<s>haridrā</s>) equal to the total. || 30 ||
All this should be ground with menstrual fluid and plantain juice;
In a sand-bath apparatus (<s>vālukāyantra</s>). || 31 ||
At the end of the day, having formed a ball, cook it

children.text: dinaṃ mandāgninā taṃ vai samuddhṛtya vicūrṇayet |
children.translated_text: With a gentle fire for one day; then extract and powder it;

children.text: cūrṇāṃśaṃ gandhakaṃ dattvā garbhayantre tryahaṃ pacet || 32 ||
children.translated_text: Adding an equal portion of sulfur to the powder, cook in a sealed vessel (<s>garbhayantra</s>) for three days. || 32 ||
With husk fire, gently — the calcined mercury (<s>bhasmasūtaka</s>) is produced.
Third method of calcination of mercury.
Mercury, three parts; one part copper powder. || 33 ||
Pure
Grind with acids for one day; wash and form a pellet;
From <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), prepare the washed essence, equal to the pellet. || 34 ||
All that should be ground for three days with juices of <s>cakramarda</s> (Cassia tora) leaves;
That ball, placed in a sealed vessel (<s>garbhayantra</s>), heated with husk fire for three days — || 35 ||
In cowdung fire for one day and night — it attains the state of ash (<s>bhasma</s>).
Or
Fourth method of calcination of mercury.

children.text: śuddhasūtaṃ vyomasattvaṃ suvarṇaṃ ca samaṃ samam || 36 ||
children.translated_text: Pure mercury, mica (<s>vyomasattva</s>) essence, and gold — in equal parts. || 36 ||
Adding an equal amount of <s>biḍa</s> (a type of salt), grind with plantain juice for one day;
Then grind for two days with equal seeds of divine herbs. || 37 ||
Cook it placed in a sealed vessel; it dies (calcines) in the <s>puṭa</s> (heating cycle) as before.
Characteristics of the sealed vessel (<s>garbhayantra</s>).
It should be four finger-breadths in length and three finger-breadths in diameter. || 38 ||

children.text: mṛṇmayaṃ sampuṭaṃ kṛtvā chāyāśuṣkaṃ ca kārayet |
children.translated_text: Having made a clay container with a lid (<s>sampuṭa</s>), it should be shade-dried;
Salt should be one-twentieth part, and one part of <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium). || 39 ||
All should be ground with water; with that, the interior of the container
Should be smeared, and the mercury sealed therein — this constitutes the <s>garbhayantra</s>. || 40 ||
Fifth method of calcination of mercury.
<s>Vimalā</s> (a herb) and pure mercury in equal parts, with juice of <s>nirguṇḍikā</s> (Vitex negundo) —
Grind for three days; then place it in a glass bottle (<s>kācakūpī</s>). || 41 ||
In the absence of a glass bottle, seal it in a distillation vessel (<s>śrāvasampuṭa</s>);
Cook in a sand-bath apparatus for four <s>yāmas</s> — it will be calcined (dead). || 42 ||
Sixth method of calcination of mercury.
The washed essence from <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), and an equal amount of pure sulfur,
And pure mercury equal to both combined — grind for one day with juice of <s>nirguṇḍikā</s>. || 43 ||
All that, ground into a ball, sealed in a diamond crucible, should be cooked
For one day in a sand-bath apparatus — it becomes calcined, of red color. || 44 ||
Seventh method of calcination of mercury.
Sulfur in equal amount should be placed above and below the pure mercury
In the belly of a heated crucible; then the juice of <s>kākamācī</s> (black nightshade) — || 45 ||
Adding four times the amount of the two, covering with a plate, cook gently
In a gradual fire (<s>kramāgni</s>) in a sand-bath apparatus for four <s>yāmas</s> — it will be calcined. || 46 ||
Eighth method of calcination of mercury.

children.text: snuhyā vā hemavallyā vā kṣīraiḥ śuddharasaṃ dinam |
children.translated_text: With the milk of <s>snuhī</s> (Euphorbia) or <s>hemavallī</s> (golden creeper), grind pure mercury for one day;
Add equal sulfur, place in a sealed vessel, and calcine with <s>puṭa</s> (heating cycle). || 47 ||
As before, by gradual process, the calcined product should be employed in formulations.
Ninth method of calcination of mercury.
Equal to pure mercury: <s>guñjā</s> (rosary pea), lac (<s>lākṣā</s>), wool (<s>ūrṇā</s>), honey, and borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>). || 48 ||
All that should be ground with juices of <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> (Eclipta) for one day;
Sealed in a diamond crucible and heated — it becomes calcined, moon-like in appearance. || 49 ||
Tenth method of calcination of mercury.
With juices of <s>kīṭamāriṇī</s> (insect-killer plant), or with juices of <s>ajamodā</s> (celery),
Or with juices of <s>ahimārī</s> (snake-killer plant), or with juices of <s>śvetāṅkula</s> — || 50 ||
Grind pure mercury with equal sulfur for three days;
Seal in a clay container and heat in cowdung fire day and night. || 51 ||
Or cook with husk fire; in three days it surely becomes calcined.
Eleventh method of calcination of mercury.
Pure mercury and calcined diamond (<s>vajra</s>) in equal parts, in a heated mortar — || 52 ||
Grind with juices of <s>haṃsapādī</s> (goosefoot plant); after three days, extract it;
Coat the diamond crucible with seeds of divine herbs. || 53 ||
Seal the previously [prepared] mercury therein; with husk fire for three days
Cook; then extract, and [add] an equal amount of pure mercury. || 54 ||
Combine and grind firmly for three days with juices of <s>haṃsapādī</s>;
Cook that ball as before — it becomes beautifully calcined. || 55 ||
Statement by extension regarding the method of calcination of diamond etc.
The calcination of diamond, mica, and the eight metals, as described in the <s>Rasakhaṇḍa</s> (Mercury Section),
(Transmutation Section), should likewise be understood for <s>rasāyana</s>. || 56 ||
Or in the <s>Vādikhaṇḍa</s>
Qualities of calcined mercury.
Mercury thus calcined becomes the supreme nectar —
For them,
Those who serve it constantly and firmly,
It swiftly makes the body of heavenly women
Fit for play, supremely beautiful, and eternal. || 57 ||

children.text:
iti śrīpārvatīputranityanāthasiddhaviracite rasaratnākare rasāyanakhaṇḍe
                    rasa- māraṇaṃ nāma prathamopadeśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first teaching called 'Calcination of Mercury' in the <s>Rasāyanakhaṇḍa</s> of the <s>Rasaratnākara</s> composed by <s>Śrī Nityanātha Siddha</s>, son of <s>Pārvatī</s>.
Second teaching.
By righteous ones, devoted to <s>Śiva</s>, by great adepts — royal practitioners —
Through the proper [use of] divine <s>rasāyana</s>, constantly, up to the boundary of the end of the age (<s>kalpa</s>),
Through an infinite accumulation of merit; and since liberation (<s>mukti</s>) arises from this existence,
The body is to be protected
I shall expound that supremely wondrous, bliss-producing, sovereignty-granting [teaching] for the wise.
Method of consuming mica for making the body a receptacle (<s>kṣetrīkaraṇa</s>).
First, one should consume mica (<s>abhraka</s>) that has been calcined and made into nectar (<s>amṛtīkṛta</s>),
One <s>niṣka</s> (gold coin weight) each month, for the purpose of making [the body] a receptacle. || 2 ||
Since mica is the field (<s>kṣetra</s>) for mercury, therefore one should undertake <s>rasāyana</s>;
Without making the body a receptacle, mercury, even if nectarized, turns to poison. || 3 ||
How can the fruit of a good seed succeed in barren soil? Similarly,
<s>Vajrapañjara Rasa</s> (Diamond-cage Mercury Formula).
Prepare equal parts of the ashes of diamond (<s>vajra</s>) and mercury. || 4 ||

children.text: sūtapādaṃ mṛtaṃ svarṇaṃ sarvaṃ mardyaṃ dināvadhi |
children.translated_text: One-quarter part of calcined gold relative to mercury — grind all for one day
With juices of <s>haṃsapādī</s>; form that into a ball, seal it, and calcine with <s>puṭa</s>. || 5 ||
Grind again with the milk of <s>arka</s> (Calotropis); cook similarly in an elephant-dung <s>puṭa</s>;
Consume [starting from] the size of a mustard seed, gradually increasing to the weight of a <s>māṣa</s>. || 6 ||
This mercury, <s>Vajrapañjara</s> (Diamond-cage), is the refuge of practitioners.
<s>Citraka</s> (Plumbago), fresh ginger (<s>ārdraka</s>), rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>), <s>mṛtatakṣṇi</s> (?), and <s>suvarcala</s> (a type of salt) — || 7 ||

children.text: samaṃ sarvaṃ sadā cānu bhakṣyaṃ syātkrāmaṇe hitam |
children.translated_text: All in equal parts, should always be eaten as an accompaniment — it aids in assimilation.
By the practice of six months, one would live as long as the moon and stars endure. || 8 ||
Free from wrinkles and grey hair, with a divine body and great strength.
<s>Vajreśvara Rasa</s> (Lord-of-Diamond Mercury Formula).
From the calcined mercury, one should prepare one-twelfth part of calcined <s>vajra</s> (diamond/thunderbolt). (9)

children.text: dvābhyāṃ tulyaṃ mṛtaṃ kāntaṃ kāntatulyaṃ mṛtābhrakam |
children.translated_text: Calcined <s>kānta</s> (iron/loadstone) equal to twice that, and calcined <s>abhraka</s> (mica) equal to the <s>kānta</s>;
all of this should be ground with juices of <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> (Eclipta alba) and macerated for three days. (10)
Three days with juices of <s>gokṣuraka</s> (Tribulus terrestris); then one should lick one <s>māṣa</s> (measure) with honey.
This <s>rasa</s> (mercurial preparation) called <s>Vajreśvara</s> makes the body of men diamond-like. (11)
In four months it destroys old age; one lives for a day of <s>Brahmā</s>, indeed.
One should powder the five parts of <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> equal to <s>triphalā</s>. (12)

children.text: palaikaṃ madhunā lehyaṃ krāmakaṃ paramaṃ rase |
children.translated_text: One <s>pala</s> (measure) should be licked with honey — this is the supreme <s>krāmaka</s> (adjuvant) for the <s>rasa</s>.
<s>Vajradhārā-rasa</s>:

children.text: vajrasūtābhrahemnāṃ tu bhasma śuddhaṃ tu mākṣikam || 13 ||
children.translated_text: Purified <s>bhasma</s> (ash/calx) of <s>vajra</s> (diamond), <s>sūta</s> (mercury), <s>abhraka</s> (mica), <s>hema</s> (gold), and <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), (13)
equal parts, should be ground firmly for seven days with juices of divine herbs.
Having sealed it, one should cook it for three days in a <s>vālukā-yantra</s> (sand-bath apparatus), then again (14)
having extracted it, it should be macerated for three days with juices of <s>bhṛṅga</s> (Eclipta), <s>sarpākṣī</s> (Ophiorrhiza), etc.
One should lick one <s>māṣa</s> of <s>Vajradhārā-rasa</s> with honey and ghee. (15)
By the application for six months, a man becomes equal to <s>Rudra</s>.
Freed from wrinkles and grey hair, with the speed of wind, of great strength. (16)
<s>Punarnavā</s> (Boerhavia diffusa), <s>bhṛṅga</s> (Eclipta), <s>tila</s> (sesame), and <s>vājīgandhā</s> (Ashwagandha) in equal parts,
an equal amount of sugar should be added; one should eat one <s>pala</s> of the powder. (17)
<s>Bhairava-rasa</s>:

children.text: suvarṇaṃ pāradaṃ kāntaṃ mṛtaṃ sarvaṃ samaṃ bhavet |
children.translated_text: Gold, mercury, and <s>kānta</s> (loadstone), all calcined, should be in equal parts.
It should be macerated for three days with juices from the roots of <s>śatāvarī</s> (Asparagus racemosus). (18)
Three days with decoctions of <s>triphalā</s>, three days with juices of <s>bhṛṅga</s> (Eclipta);
the macerated <s>Bhairava-rasa</s> should be consumed with honey and ghee. (19)
One <s>māṣa</s> daily for one year — one lives as long as the moon, sun, and stars.
Root-powder of <s>śatāvarī</s> combined with milk of a black she-goat, (20)
one should drink one <s>pala</s> as the adjuvant — the supreme <s>krāmaka</s>, most beneficial.
<s>Śilāvīra-rasa</s>:
<s>Rasa-bhasma</s> (mercury calx), an equal amount of <s>gandha</s> (sulfur), <s>śilājatu</s> (bitumen), and <s>amlavetasa</s> (sorrel), (21)
all should be ground for one <s>yāma</s> (watch, ~3 hours); it should be licked with honey and ghee.
One <s>niṣka</s> (measure) daily for one year — <s>Śilāvīra</s>, the great <s>rasa</s>, (22)
swiftly destroys the onset of old age; one lives for three hundred years.
Half a <s>pala</s> of <s>muśalī</s> (Curculigo orchioides) powder should be drunk with <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> juice. (23)
Or with <s>dhātrīphala</s> (āmalaka/gooseberry) juice — this is the <s>krāmaka</s> adjuvant.
<s>Amṛtārṇava-rasa</s> (Ocean of Nectar):
Purified mercury should be ground for three days with juices of <s>meghanāda</s> (Solanum indicum). (24)

children.text: viḍaṅgaṃ dviniśaṃ vyoṣaṃ samaṃ cūrṇaṃ prakalpayet |
children.translated_text: <s>Viḍaṅga</s> (Embelia ribes), <s>dviniśa</s> (turmeric), and <s>vyoṣa</s> (the three pungents) — equal powder should be prepared.

children.text: āragvadhasya mūlaṃ tu cūrṇasya dviguṇaṃ bhavet || 25 ||
children.translated_text: The root of <s>āragvadha</s> (Cassia fistula) should be double the quantity of the powder. (25)

children.text: cūrṇasya dviguṇaṃ cājyaṃ kṣaudraṃ caiva caturguṇam |
children.translated_text: Ghee double the quantity of the powder, and honey four times the quantity;

children.text: sarvaṃ pūrvarase kṣiptvā mṛdvagnau cālayan pacet || 26 ||
children.translated_text: all should be put into the previous <s>rasa</s> and cooked on a gentle fire while stirring. (26)
One should eat one <s>karṣa</s> (measure) of that bolus — this is <s>Amṛtārṇava</s>.
For one year it destroys old age; one lives for three hundred years. (27)
One should drink one <s>karṣa</s> of <s>bākucī</s> (Psoralea corylifolia) powder with <s>dhātrīphala</s> juice.
<s>Udayāditya-rasa</s> (Rising Sun):
Sulfur double the quantity of mercury — all purified — should be ground together (28)
in a mortar with juices of <s>muṇḍī</s> (Sphaeranthus indicus) and fresh ginger, for three weeks, repeatedly.
An equal quantity of purified copper should be confined in a <s>sampuṭa</s> (sealed crucible) with it. (29)
It should be wrapped in a piece of cloth and coated externally with <s>vajramṛttikā</s> (adamantine clay),
dried and properly cooked in a <s>gajapuṭa</s> (elephant-grade incineration). (30)
Having extracted the <s>sampuṭa</s>, it should be powdered and macerated for three days with juices of <s>devadālī</s> (Luffa echinata).
It should be macerated separately for three days each with juices of <s>bhaṅgī</s> (Cannabis) and <s>punarnavā</s> (Boerhavia). (31)
An equal quantity of dry ginger powder should be added, combined with honey and ghee,
and two <s>māṣas</s> should be licked daily for up to one year. (32)
This <s>rasa</s> called <s>Udayāditya</s> (Rising Sun) is the supreme destroyer of old age and death.
Equal quantities of powder of <s>punarnavā</s>, <s>devadālī</s>, and <s>bhṛṅga</s> (Eclipta), (33)
one should lick one <s>karṣa</s> with honey and ghee — this is the supreme <s>krāmaṇa</s> adjuvant.
<s>Gaganeśvara-rasa</s> (Lord of the Sky):

children.text: pārado gaganaṃ kāntaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ ca māritaṃ samam || 34 ||
children.translated_text: Mercury, <s>gagana</s> (mica), <s>kānta</s> (loadstone), and <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (iron), all calcined, in equal parts, (34)
should be macerated for three days in the shade with juices of <s>bhṛṅga</s> and <s>dhātrīphala</s> (gooseberry).
Equal quantities of sugar, honey, and ghee — all should be sealed in a vessel. (35)

children.text: dhānyarāśau sthitaṃ māsaṃ tato niṣkatrayaṃ samam |
children.translated_text: Kept in a heap of grain for one month, then three <s>niṣkas</s> in equal measure
should be consumed, and milk should be drunk; one <s>karṣa</s> of <s>triphalā</s> as adjuvant. (36)
At night one should chew dry ginger and long pepper — in one year one becomes immortal.
The hero lives for a day of <s>Brahmā</s> — this is the <s>rasa</s> called <s>Gaganeśvara</s>. (37)
<s>Vaṭeśvara-rasa</s> (Lord of the Banyan):
Sulfur and purified mercury in equal parts should be ground for three days with banyan tree milk.
It should be cooked on a fire of banyan wood in an earthen vessel for five <s>yāmas</s> (watches). (38)
Adding banyan milk repeatedly, it should be stirred with that very wood.
Having extracted it, it should be macerated for three days with juices of <s>devadālī</s> leaves. (39)
In the warm season, one <s>guñjā</s> (measure) combined with betel leaves
should always be consumed, increasing with the waxing moon, up to sixteen <s>guñjās</s>. (40)
Powder of <s>uttaravāruṇī</s> (Boerhavia), <s>bākucī</s> (Psoralea), and <s>devadālī</s>;
one should lick one <s>karṣa</s> with honey and ghee — this is the <s>krāmaka</s> adjuvant. (41)
In one year it destroys old age; one lives for three hundred years.
This <s>rasa</s> called <s>Vaṭeśvara</s> makes the body of men diamond-like. (42)
<s>Acaleśvara-rasa</s> (Lord of the Mountain):

children.text: mṛtaṃ sūtaṃ śuddhagandhaṃ triphalāṃ gugugluṃ samam |
children.translated_text: Calcined mercury, purified sulfur, <s>triphalā</s>, and <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium resin), in equal parts,
all mixed with <s>vātāri</s> (castor) oil — one should always lick one <s>karṣa</s>. (43)
In six months it destroys old age; one lives for three days of <s>Brahmā</s>.
By his urine and feces, copper becomes gold. (44)

children.text: ajasya vṛṣaṇaṃ pācyaṃ gavāṃ kṣīreṇa taṃ niśi |
children.translated_text: The testicle of a goat should be cooked in cow's milk overnight;
combined with sugar, one should drink it as adjuvant — this is <s>Acaleśvara-rasa</s>. (45)
<s>Parameśvara-rasa</s> (Supreme Lord):

children.text: rasaṃ vajraṃ svarṇakānte muṇḍaṃ ca māritaṃ samam |
children.translated_text: Mercury, <s>vajra</s> (diamond), gold, <s>kānta</s> (loadstone), and <s>muṇḍa</s> (tin), all calcined, in equal parts,
<s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite) and purified sulfur — all with juices of <s>jambīra</s> (citron) (46)
should be ground in a mortar for seven days; that ball should be sealed and incinerated

children.text: bhūdhare dinamekaṃ tu khyātaḥ siddharasaḥ paraḥ || 47 ||
children.translated_text: in a <s>bhūdhara</s> furnace for one day — this is the renowned supreme <s>siddha-rasa</s>. (47)
One <s>māṣa</s> should be licked with honey — in one year it destroys death and old age.
A man of divine body, accomplished, becomes equal to <s>Viṣṇu</s> in prowess. (48)
The root of white <s>punarnavā</s> (Boerhavia diffusa), ground with milk, should always be drunk,
or eaten with sugar — this is the <s>krāmaka</s> for the supreme
<s>Gandhāmṛta-rasa</s> (Sulfur Nectar):
Double the quantity of calcined mercury, purified sulfur should be mixed.
Having ground it for one day with juices of <s>kanyakā</s> (aloe), it should be sealed. (50)
It should be cooked for one day with honey; one <s>niṣka</s> should be licked with honey.
The <s>rasa</s> called <s>Gandhāmṛta</s> — in one year it conquers death. (51)
<s>Bhṛṅgarāja</s> with its root should be shade-dried and powdered.
An equal quantity of <s>triphalā</s> powder; sugar equal to the total. (52)
All combined together, one <s>pala</s> should be eaten as adjuvant.
<s>Kālakaṇṭaka-rasa</s> (Death's Thorn):

children.text: pāradābhraṃ mṛtaṃ tulyaṃ dvābhyāṃ tulyaṃ tu gandhakam || 53 ||
children.translated_text: Calcined mercury and <s>abhraka</s> (mica) in equal parts; sulfur equal to both combined. (53)
All of this should be ground for seven days with juices of <s>bhṛṅga</s> (Eclipta).
(castor) oil, it should then be consumed. (54)
Having macerated six times with <s>aṅkulī</s>
One <s>māṣa</s> measure for one year — this <s>rasa</s> is <s>Kālakaṇṭaka</s>.
Having ground <s>karañja</s> (Pongamia) leaves, one should drink them with cow's milk as adjuvant. (55)
Freed from old age and death, a man lives for a day of <s>Brahmā</s>.
<s>Amṛteśa-rasa</s> (Lord of Nectar):
Calcined mercury, <s>abhraka</s> (mica), <s>kānta</s> (loadstone), <s>viṣa</s> (poison/aconite), <s>tāpya</s> (pyrite), and <s>śilājatu</s> (bitumen), (56)
in equal parts — three <s>guñjās</s> should always be licked with honey and ghee.
In six months it destroys old age; a man lives for a day of <s>Brahmā</s>. (57)
<s>Aśvagandhā</s> (Withania somnifera) root-powder, equal to seven parts of ghee,

children.text: bhāgāṣṭakaṃ guḍaṃ tasmin kṣipedbhāgaṃ ca pippalīm || 58 ||
children.translated_text: eight parts of <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery) should be added to that, and one part of <s>pippalī</s> (long pepper). (58)

children.text: mṛdvagninā ca tatsarvaṃ piṇḍitaṃ bhakṣayet palam |
children.translated_text: All of that should be formed into a bolus on gentle fire and one <s>pala</s> should be eaten.
This is the <s>krāmaka</s> of <s>Amṛteśa</s> for the accomplishment of the king of <s>rasas</s>. (59)
<s>Rasavīra-mahārasa</s> (Great Mercury Hero):
Three times the quantity of purified mercury, purified sulfur should be combined.
Powder of iron scales, equal to the mercury, should be added. (60)
All should be ground for three days with the milky sap of <s>snuhī</s> (Euphorbia) and <s>arka</s> (Calotropis).
When dried, it should be sealed and cooked on cow-dung fire day and night. (61)

children.text: tataśca ṭaṅkaṇaṃ kācaṃ dattvā ruddhvā dhameddṛḍham |
children.translated_text: Then <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax) and glass should be added, sealed, and blown firmly (with bellows).
— <s>Rasavīra</s>, the great <s>rasa</s>. (62)
One <s>guñjā</s> should be eaten with honey
In one year it destroys old age; one lives as long as the moon and stars.
<s>Muśalī</s> (Curculigo) root-powder should be drunk with <s>guñjā</s>-leaf juices. (63)

children.text: chāgīmūtreṇa vā taṃ vai karṣaikaṃ krāmakaṃ param |
children.translated_text: Or with she-goat's urine — one <s>karṣa</s> is the supreme <s>krāmaka</s>.
<s>Kāñcāyana-rasa</s> (Golden):
Sulfur equal to the calcined mercury, with juices of <s>kākamācī</s> (Solanum nigrum) for one day, (64)
ground and sealed, it should be cooked on cow-dung fire day and night.
It should be ground for one day with juices of divine herb leaves, then sealed. (65)
Having been blown (with bellows) and extracted, an equal quantity of calcined gold,
combined together, should be licked with ghee — one <s>māṣa</s> for up to one year. (66)

children.text: jarāṃ mṛtyuṃ nihantyāśu satyaṃ kāñcāyano rasaḥ |
children.translated_text: It swiftly destroys old age and death — truly, this is <s>Kāñcāyana-rasa</s>.
Powder derived from <s>dhātrīphala</s> (gooseberry) should be macerated with <s>kākamācī</s> juices. (67)
One <s>karṣa</s> should be eaten with honey — this is the supreme <s>krāmaka</s> adjuvant.
<s>Parānanda-rasa</s> (Supreme Bliss):
Calcined mercury, <s>abhraka</s> (mica), and sulfur in equal parts, for up to seven days, (68)
should be ground with juices of <s>śigru</s> (Moringa) root; that ball should be placed inside a vessel,
sealed and cooked lightly with <s>śāka</s> (teak) wood for one day. (69)

children.text: parānando raso nāma ghṛtairniṣkaṃ sadā lihet |
children.translated_text: The <s>rasa</s> called <s>Parānanda</s> — one <s>niṣka</s> should always be licked with ghee.
For one day, <s>kuṣṭha</s> (Saussurea) should be properly decocted with <s>triphalā</s> decoction. (70)
When dried and powdered, one <s>karṣa</s> should be licked with honey and ghee as adjuvant.
By the application for one year, one lives as long as the moon and stars. (71)
<s>Mahākāla-rasa</s> (Great Time/Death):
Calcined mercury and <s>abhraka</s> (mica) in equal parts; calcined iron equal to both combined.
Purified sulfur in the proportion of the iron — it should be macerated for seven days. (72)
All of this with decoctions of <s>triphalā</s>, <s>bhṛṅga</s> (Eclipta), <s>śigru</s> (Moringa), and <s>citraka</s> (Plumbago);
each should be macerated separately seven times in succession with their respective juices. (73)
Having been macerated seven times with decoctions of <s>kaṭukī</s> (Picrorhiza), it should be powdered again.
Powder of long pepper equal to the powder, with an equal quantity of aged <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery), (74)
all combined together, one <s>niṣka</s> should be eaten for up to one year.
The <s>rasa</s> called <s>Mahākāla</s> is terrifying to old age and death. (75)
Leaves of <s>tila</s> (sesame) and <s>koraṇṭa</s> (Barleria) should be eaten with jaggery as adjuvant.
<s>Hemaparpaṭaka-rasa</s> (Gold Flake):
Iron flake equal to the calcined mercury. (76)
Sulfur three times the mercury — all with juices of divine herbs;

children.text: marditaṃ taddinaṃ ruddhvā dhmāto baddho bhavedrasaḥ || 77 ||
children.translated_text: ground for one day and sealed, when blown (with bellows), the <s>rasa</s> becomes bound. (77)

children.text: tasmin pādaṃ mṛtaṃ svarṇaṃ kṣiptvā vahnyārdrakadravaiḥ |
children.translated_text: To that, adding one quarter part of calcined gold, with juices of <s>vahnyādraka</s> (fiery ginger),
it should be ground for one <s>yāma</s> and then powdered with <s>vyoṣa</s> (three pungents), cumin, and rock salt. (78)

children.text: tulyaṃ pūrvarasaṃ tulyaṃ niṣkaikaikaṃ ca bhakṣayet |
children.translated_text: Equal to the previous <s>rasa</s> in equal measure, one <s>niṣka</s> should be consumed.
It swiftly destroys old age and death — this is <s>Hemaparpaṭaka-rasa</s>. (79)
<s>Aśvagandhā</s> and an equal quantity of <s>yaṣṭī</s> (licorice), macerated for one day with <s>dhātrīphala</s> juice,
should be licked — one <s>pala</s> with honey — this is the supreme <s>krāmaka</s>. (80)
<s>Śrīkaṇṭha-rasa</s> (Beautiful Throat):

children.text: svarṇatārārkakāntaṃ ca tīkṣṇaṃ vā māritaṃ samam |
children.translated_text: Gold, silver, sun-stone (<s>sūryakānta</s>), and <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (iron), or all calcined in equal parts,
the essence of dark <s>abhraka</s> (mica) and <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), each equal to the gold, (81)
all of this sealed and blown; that <s>khoṭa</s> (alloy) with calcined mercury

children.text: samaṃ sūnānmṛtaṃ vajraṃ pādāṃśaṃ tatra yojayet || 82 ||
children.translated_text: in equal parts; calcined <s>vajra</s> (diamond) in one-quarter proportion should be added to it. (82)
All should be ground in a heated mortar with juices of <s>jambīra</s> (citron).
seal it for one day, then heat it on a <s>bhūdhara</s> (earth-furnace) for a day. || 83 ||

children.text: uddhṛtya gandhakaṃ tulyaṃ dattvā ruddhvā dhameddrutam |
children.translated_text: Having extracted it, add an equal amount of <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur), seal it, and smelt it quickly.
That powder should always be licked in a dose of one <s>māṣa</s> (approximately 1 gram) with honey and ghee. || 84 ||
This <s>rasa</s> (mercury preparation) named <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s> bestows the power of <s>khecara</s> (moving through the sky);
with continuous use for one year, one lives until the end of the <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic age). || 85 ||
By his urine and feces, all base metals become gold.

children.text: palaikaṃ gandhakaṃ kṣīraiḥ krāmakaṃ cānu pāyayet || 86 ||
children.translated_text: One <s>pala</s> (approximately 48 grams) of <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur) should be drunk with milk, and <s>krāmaka</s> (an adjuvant) should be taken afterwards. || 86 ||
<s>Khecarabaddha Rasa</s> (Mercury Bound with Khecara):
One part of purified <s>tāmra</s> (copper), twelve parts of purified <s>rasa</s> (mercury),
and three parts of the essence of <s>bhūnāga</s> (lead)—combine all in one place. || 87 ||
Grind everything in a heated mortar with the juices of <s>jambīra</s> (citrus) for one day.

children.text: tatsarvaṃ kacchape yantre kṣiptvā tatraiva gandhakam || 88 ||
children.translated_text: Place all of it in a <s>kacchapa yantra</s> (tortoise-shaped apparatus), and into that same vessel add <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur), || 88 ||

children.text: kāsamardarasaiḥ piṣṭaṃ tulyaṃ dattvā nirudhya ca |
children.translated_text: ground with the juices of <s>kāsamarda</s> (Cassia occidentalis), in equal quantity; seal it,
and cook in a <s>puṭa</s> (sealed heating) until fully digested. In this manner, digest six times the amount of <s>gandhaka</s>. || 89 ||
Digest it progressively by the sequential method; then extract and grind
for one <s>yāma</s> (three hours) with juices of <s>jambīra</s> (citrus). Then add <s>abhraka</s> (mica) devoid of luster (<s>niścandra</s>), || 90 ||
equal to <s>amlavetasa</s> (Garcinia pedunculata), ground, to the mercury preparation.
Add one-sixteenth part in a heated mortar, along with sour <s>caṇaka</s> (chickpea extract) and <s>tālaka</s> (orpiment), || 91 ||

children.text: kāsīsaṃ ca daśāṃśena dattvā mardyaṃ dināvadhi |
children.translated_text: and <s>kāsīsa</s> (green vitriol) in one-tenth proportion, and grind for a full day.
Place all of it in a fired crucible (<s>pakvamūṣā</s>) and bind it with cloth. || 92 ||
Cook it in a <s>dolāyantra</s> (swing apparatus) with <s>sāranāla</s> (distilled liquor) over mild fire for three days.
Extract it and wash with hot <s>kāñjika</s> (sour gruel). If it is digested, || 93 ||
if undigested, cook it in the apparatus called <s>kacchapa</s> (tortoise) with <s>biḍa</s> (a salt compound).
In this manner, <s>gagana</s> (tin/mica) equal in quantity to mercury should be repeatedly digested. || 94 ||
Gold leaves smeared with peacock bile—
add them in one-sixty-fourth proportion and grind in a mortar. || 95 ||
Steam in the apparatus as before; when digested, add gold.

children.text: ityevaṃ ṣoḍaśāṃśaṃ tu svarṇaṃ jāryaṃ rasasya vai || 96 ||
children.translated_text: In this manner, gold amounting to one-sixteenth of the mercury should be digested. || 96 ||

children.text: tato jāryaṃ mṛtaṃ vajraṃ ṣoḍaśāṃśaṃ ca hemavat |
children.translated_text: Then digest calcined <s>vajra</s> (diamond) in one-sixteenth proportion, like gold,
combined with <s>tālaka</s> (orpiment), <s>kāsīsa</s> (green vitriol), and <s>jambīra</s> (citrus)—grind thoroughly after that. || 97 ||
Then grind that mercury with juices of divine herbs for three days.
Sealed in a diamond-crucible, it should be smelted; when it becomes bound, powder it again. || 98 ||
Consume it in a dose of one <s>guñjā</s> (approximately 0.12 grams) together with honey and sugar.
This mercury, bound as <s>khecara</s>, conquers death within six months. || 99 ||
One becomes free from wrinkles and gray hair, possessing great strength and valor.
Soak for seven days with juices of <s>mṛṅga</s> (Moringa), <s>nīlī</s> (indigo), <s>muṇḍī</s> (Sphaeranthus), and the three fruits (<s>triphalā</s>). || 100 ||
Prepare with honey and ghee, and lick one <s>karṣa</s> (approximately 12 grams) afterwards.
<s>Svayam Agni Rasa</s> (Self-Igniting Mercury):
Take purified mercury (<s>śuddhasūta</s>) and <s>gandha</s> (sulfur) in two parts; make a <s>kañjala</s> (black compound) in a mortar. || 101 ||

children.text: tayostulyaṃ kāntacūrṇaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ vā muṇḍameva vā |
children.translated_text: Add to those an equal amount of <s>kānta</s> (magnetite) powder, or <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (iron), or <s>muṇḍa</s> (another iron variety).
Combine everything in one mortar and grind with juices of <s>kanyakā</s> (aloe). || 102 ||
After one day, form it into a ball and place it in a copper vessel.
Cover it with castor leaves; in half a <s>yāma</s> (one and a half hours) it will become extremely hot. || 103 ||
Place it in a heap of grain; after two days, extract it.
<s>Kanyā</s> (aloe), <s>bhṛṅgī</s> (Clerodendrum), <s>kākamācī</s> (black nightshade), <s>muṇḍī</s> (Sphaeranthus), <s>nirguṇḍī</s> (Vitex negundo), <s>citraka</s> (Plumbago), || 104 ||
<s>koraṇṭa</s> (Barleria), <s>bākucī</s> (Psoralea), <s>brāhmī</s> (Bacopa), <s>sahadevī</s> (Sida), <s>punarnavā</s> (Boerhavia),
<s>śālmalī</s> (Bombax), <s>vijayā</s> (cannabis), <s>dhūrtā</s> (Datura)—with the juices of each of these separately, || 105 ||
it should be steeped seven times with each, seven times with each, and seven times with decoctions of the three fruits (<s>triphalā</s>).
The steeped preparation should be powdered with <s>jātīphala</s> (nutmeg) and <s>lavaṅga</s> (clove). || 106 ||
<s>Trikaṭu</s> (three pungents), <s>triphalā</s> (three fruits), and <s>elā</s> (cardamom)—powder these nine in equal parts.

children.text: taccūrṇaṃ pūrvacūrṇaṃ ca samaṃ kṣaudreṇa karṣakam || 107 ||
children.translated_text: Mix that powder with the previous powder in equal measure, with honey, one <s>karṣa</s> (dose). || 107 ||
Lick it daily for one year to pacify the effects of aging.
This, named <s>Svayam Agni Rasa</s> (Self-Igniting Mercury), has come from the mouths of the <s>Siddha</s>-s (perfected beings). || 108 ||
Lick half a <s>pala</s> of powder of sesame and <s>aśvagandhā</s> (Withania somnifera) with honey.

<s>Nirguṇḍī</s> (Vitex negundo), <s>nīlikā</s> (indigo), <s>vajrī</s> (Euphorbia), <s>brahmadaṇḍī</s> (Argemone), <s>tridaṇḍikā</s> (a plant), || 109 ||

children.text: kāntābhraṃ kāñcanaṃ sūtaṃ kṛtvā golaṃ tu veśayet |
children.translated_text: <s>Kānta</s>, <s>abhraka</s>, gold, and mercury, made into a ball, should be placed
on the bamboo-tip, consecrated with <s>mantras</s> — that becomes a touch-transmuter. (55)
At the western gate of <s>Śrīśaila</s>, the deity named <s>Brahmeśvareśvara</s>.
That <s>liṅga</s> is said to transmute by touch; likewise <s>Durgā</s> there. (56)

children.text: navamaṃ yattu sopānaṃ nadyāṃ tattādṛśaṃ sthitam |
children.translated_text: The ninth step in the river — that too has such properties.
At the door of the deity, one should observe a <s>mudga</s> (mung bean)-colored substance. (57)
To the southwest of <s>Brahmeśvara</s> is situated a tamarind grove.

children.text: tasmin vane sthitaṃ kuṇḍaṃ tatra tiṣṭhati caṇḍikā || 58 ||
children.translated_text: In that grove is a pool where <s>Caṇḍikā</s> (fierce goddess) resides. (58)
Standing on one foot beneath a <s>ciñcā</s> (tamarind) tree, one should collect leaves from that tree,

children.text: baddhvā vastre kṣipetkuṇḍe snānaṃ tatra samācaret || 59 ||
children.translated_text: tie them in cloth, cast them in the pool, and bathe there. (59)

children.text: snānānte poṭalī grāhyā sarve matsyā bhavanti te |
children.translated_text: After bathing, the bundle should be collected — all those become fish.
They should be cooked with that very wood; the throat, tail, and head should be discarded. (60)
One portion should be offered to the deity, the second to a guest,

children.text: tṛtīyaṃ sādhako bhuktvā kṣaṇaṃ bhavati mūrcchitaḥ || 61 ||
children.translated_text: the third the practitioner should eat — for a moment he becomes faint. (61)
Instantly, <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment) arises — one sees the interior of the earth.
One attains freedom from old age and death, and is not assailed even by the gods. (62)
To the north of <s>Alampura</s>, there is a village called <s>Bhīmapāduka</s>.

children.text: tasya grāmasya pārśve tu hastamātraṃ khanedbhuvam || 63 ||
children.translated_text: Near that village, one should dig the ground to a depth of one hand-span. (63)

children.text: pāṣāṇāḥ sarpavadvakrā grāhyā sparśā bhavanti te |
children.translated_text: Stones curved like serpents should be collected — they transmute by touch.
The renowned deity called <s>Yogeśvarī</s> is at <s>Alampura</s>. (64)

children.text: devyā hyagre guhā ramyā tanmadhye nikhanedbhuvam |
children.translated_text: Before the goddess is a beautiful cave; within it one should dig.
Frog-shaped stones should be collected with cat's excrement. (65)
Mixed together and cast upon tin, that tin becomes silver.
The wise one should eat those stones combined with honey and ghee. (66)
At the northern gate of <s>Śrīśaila</s>, the deity named <s>Maheśa</s>.
A <s>Bhramara-āmra</s> (bee-mango) tree stands there; its ripe fruits (67)
when split open, bees with life emerge from within.
Having thus verified the sign, one should set aside the bees. (68)
The fruits should be cooked with milk; one should drink the milk as desired.
A slight fainting occurs; then upon awakening, one should drink again. (69)
Doing this for three weeks, a man attains a diamond-like body.
Freed from wrinkles and grey hair, one lives as long as the moon and stars. (70)
A man becomes a knower of all speech and attains the speed of wind.
With just one such mango fruit, with the bee removed,
a thousand <s>palas</s> of tin, once melted, are surely fixed. (71)
By casting it, one obtains silver — truly, as spoken by the Lord.

children.text: tatphalaṃ chidritaṃ kṛtvā utpāṭya bhramaraṃ tataḥ || 72 ||
children.translated_text: Having made a hole in that fruit and removing the bee, (72)
one <s>karṣa</s> of purified mercury and an equal amount of dark <s>abhraka</s> (mica)
should be placed inside; the opening should be sealed and coated with clay and cow-dung. (73)
of that very mango tree.
When shade-dried, it should be decocted for one <s>yāma</s> with decoctions
The pill, naturally cool, found inside the fruit, should be collected. (74)
Placed in the mouth, it grants sky-travel; it produces invisibility, of great power.
with the decoction, one becomes equal to <s>Vākpati</s> (lord of speech) and lives as long as moon and stars endure. || 75 ||

children.text: tāraṃ tāmraṃ bhujaṅgaṃ vā koṭibhāgena vedhayet |
children.translated_text: One can transmute silver, copper, or tin with one ten-millionth (<s>koṭi</s>) proportion.
Place black <s>abhraka</s> (mica) and purified mercury into that fruit as before. || 76 ||
Coat with clay and cow-dung; fire with forest <s>utpala</s> (lotus) fuel.
When naturally cooled, collect the essence; with honey and ghee, || 77 ||
always consume one <s>guñjā</s> (dose); within a month a man becomes youthful.
A hero lives for one day of <s>Brahmā</s>, endowed with the strength of nine elephants. || 78 ||
He becomes world-renowned, worthy of worship with the five offerings.
With the <s>mantra</s> '<s>Oṃ Huṃ Phaṭ</s>,' practitioners with unwavering concentration || 79 ||
should gaze toward the western direction, in the sky; at that very moment
they will see divine aerial chariots — a great conviction arises. || 80 ||
Then, heading westward, a wise person should cross a river.
A cavern is seen there; one should enter facing westward. || 81 ||
One should travel three <s>yojana</s>-s (approximately 45 km), alone, with unwavering mind.
A <s>kadalī-vana</s> (banana grove) extending five <s>yojana</s>-s becomes visible. || 82 ||
In its center, an exceedingly vast lake filled with water,
and in the middle of it, a throne resembling pure crystal. || 83 ||
Seeing it, one should fall upon the ground like a staff and recite the <s>mantra</s>:

children.text: oṃṃ hrīṃ vidyāvāgīśvarādhipataye hrīṃ oṃṃ svāhā |
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ hrīṃ Vidyā-Vāgīśvarādhipataye hrīṃ Oṃ svāhā</s>.
After bathing carefully, one should then recite one <s>lakṣa</s> (100,000) times.
One should eat as desired — roots, tubers, and fruits, etc. || 84 ||
Then above the throne, resembling pure crystal,
the Supreme Lord appears — four-armed, three-eyed. || 85 ||
Prostrating again and again with hymns, <s>mantra</s>-s, and obeisances,

children.text: varaṃ datte yatheṣṭaṃ vai sādhakasya na saṃśayaḥ || 86 ||
children.translated_text: He grants boons as desired to the practitioner — there is no doubt. || 86 ||

children.text: śatamāyatanaṃ tatra kūpānāṃ ca śataṃ nava |
children.translated_text: There are a hundred shrines there, and nine hundred wells,
an equal number of gardens, and pleasure-groves called <s>Nandana</s>. || 87 ||
Likewise, nine hundred tanks exist in the <s>Kadalī-vana</s> (banana grove),
as many cave-entrances, and wish-fulfilling trees (<s>kalpavṛkṣa</s>-s) as well. || 88 ||

children.text: tatraiva maukalī nāma yakṣiṇī prakaṭā sthitā |
children.translated_text: There, a <s>yakṣiṇī</s> (female spirit) named <s>Maukalī</s> stands in manifest form.

children.text: sā vakti bhojanaṃ dehi yadīcchasi samīhitam || 89 ||
children.translated_text: She says: 'Give me food, if you desire your wish fulfilled.' || 89 ||
Then one should reply to her: 'I shall give, O Supreme Goddess.'
A wise person should offer before her milk-rice or fruit-food. || 90 ||

children.text: sā vakti mama putro'yaṃ kṣaṇaṃ vakṣasi dhāraya |
children.translated_text: She says: 'This is my child; hold it at your chest for a moment.

children.text: yadā na muñcase bhūmau tadā siddhyaṣṭakaṃ tava || 91 ||
children.translated_text: If you do not let it drop to the ground, then the eightfold <s>siddhi</s>-s (perfections) || 91 ||
I shall give you — there is no doubt.' Or again, after the meal:
'If you let it go, I shall destroy you; therefore guard it carefully.' || 92 ||
Thus a heroic practitioner should act and attain perfection.
He should proceed northward from that lake, for half a <s>yojana</s>. || 93 ||
There exists a <s>Nandana</s> (pleasure) grove, full of flowers, called 'Divine.'
By merely smelling the flowers, hunger and thirst vanish. || 94 ||
Or one may eat from it a single fruit as appropriate.
Merely by eating it, a man's body becomes hard as <s>vajra</s> (diamond). || 95 ||
From the lake, proceeding southward for one quarter <s>yojana</s>,
one sees a <s>Nandana</s> grove full of pomegranate trees. || 96 ||
A <s>Siddha</s> who eats its fruit lives for a thousand <s>yuga</s>-s (ages).
From that lake, proceeding eastward for half a <s>krośa</s> (about 1.5 km), || 97 ||

children.text: tatra dhātrīphalaiḥ pūrṇaṃ śyāmalaṃ nandanaṃ vanam |
children.translated_text: there is a dark <s>Nandana</s> grove full of <s>dhātrī</s> (gooseberry) fruits.
By eating those fruits, one lives for three hundred <s>kalpa</s>-s. || 98 ||
From that lake, proceeding westward for one <s>yojana</s>,

children.text: tatra bilvaphalaiḥ pūrṇaṃ dṛśyate nandanaṃ vanam || 99 ||
children.translated_text: one sees a <s>Nandana</s> grove full of <s>bilva</s> (wood-apple) fruits. || 99 ||
A hero who eats its fruit lives as long as moon, sun, and stars endure.
In that delightful <s>Nandana</s> grove there is a <s>liṅga</s> (sacred emblem) of blue color. || 100 ||
Entering through the northern gate, there is a great and powerful <s>Nāga</s> (serpent).
Fierce, with seven hoods, exceedingly terrifying in appearance. || 101 ||
'<s>hruṃ</s>'—one should utter and then rise.
One should bow to it, chanting '<s>hruṃ</s>'
Then it speaks: 'I grant you the power of invisibility.' || 102 ||
'Go to the western gate; there is a divine maiden there.'
The great heroic practitioner should go there, reciting the <s>mantra</s>. || 103 ||
grant entry.
Pleased, she gives a necklace, but does not
Wearing that necklace at the throat, one becomes literally <s>Vāgīśvara</s> (Lord of Speech). || 104 ||
Then one should go to the southern gate — there, a terrifying being,
with loose hair, crooked eyes, mace in hand, sky-clad (<s>digambara</s>), || 105 ||
blue in color — seeing this <s>kṣetrapāla</s> (guardian of the field), one should recite the <s>mantra</s>:

children.text: ha hā he he haṃ hruṃkāraṃ phaṭ huṃ svāhāntameva ca || 106 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Ha hā he he haṃ hruṃkāra phaṭ huṃ svāhā</s>.' || 106 ||
By this <s>mantra</s> recitation, the <s>kṣetrapāla</s> is pleased.

children.text: dadāti khecarīṃ siddhiṃ na praveśaṃ kadācana || 107 ||
children.translated_text: He grants the <s>khecarī siddhi</s> (power of aerial movement) but never grants entry. || 107 ||
Then on the eastern side is a gate where <s>Gaṇeśvara</s> (Gaṇeśa) is present.
He is seen; the practitioner should worship Him and then enter. || 108 ||

children.text: dṛśyate divyacāpaṃ tu tathā liṅgaṃ manoharam |
children.translated_text: A divine bow is seen, and also a beautiful <s>liṅga</s>.
One should worship with the <s>Śiva mantra</s>, specifically the <s>ra</s>-syllable, and nothing else. || 109 ||
Then one should perform <s>japa</s> (recitation) there, fasting for a day and night.

children.text: pratyakṣo jāyate rudro varaṃ datte yathepsitam || 110 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rudra</s> (Śiva) appears in person and grants the desired boon. || 110 ||
Such and many more <s>siddhi</s>-s (perfections) exist in the <s>Kadalī-vana</s>.
Written in letters at the entrance there is the <s>Padmāvatī</s> cavern. || 111 ||
It is situated one <s>yojana</s> east of the lake.
Having performed emesis and purgation, the practitioner should enter there. || 112 ||
He should walk across a hundred <s>dhanuṣ</s> (bow-lengths) of desert; there, a drum (<s>mṛdaṅga</s>).
Seeing it, the hero should play it. Then <s>Padmāvatī</s> herself || 113 ||
comes and gives <s>amṛta</s> (nectar), by drinking which one becomes immortal.
Then she entreats: 'Come to my abode. || 114 ||
Accept five hundred divine maidens as your retinue.

children.text: ahaṃ patnī bhaviṣyāmi yāvadbrahmā ca jīvati || 115 ||
children.translated_text: I shall be your wife for as long as <s>Brahmā</s> lives.' || 115 ||

children.text: tadante paramaṃ sthānaṃ gacchāmo nātra saṃśayaḥ |
children.translated_text: After that, we shall go to the supreme abode — there is no doubt.
The deity <s>Kadambeśvara</s> is found in the southeastern direction. || 116 ||
At the front of the tank east of Him stands a <s>kadamba</s> tree.
Collect its leaves and anoint with mustard oil, || 117 ||
or with oil from that tree's seeds; a wise person should cook with its wood.

children.text: matsyā bhavanti te sarve tāmrapātre vinikṣipet || 118 ||
children.translated_text: Fish are produced from all of these; place them in a copper vessel. || 118 ||
Excluding the tail, spine, and head, consume with honey and ghee.
Instantly one becomes a <s>Siddha</s>, equal to <s>Rudra</s>, of great power. || 119 ||

children.text: nadīsthāne ca yo vṛkṣo vidyate kuṇḍaleśvare |
children.translated_text: At the river-place, there is a tree at <s>Kuṇḍaleśvara</s>.
By the same sequential method as before, perfection is attained — no doubt. || 120 ||
North of the deity <s>Kapoteśvara</s> stands <s>Puṣpagiri</s> (Flower Mountain).

children.text: tasya kuryāt prayatnena trivāraṃ tu pradakṣiṇam || 121 ||
children.translated_text: One should carefully circumambulate it three times. || 121 ||
Then climbing to its summit, a man attains the power of <s>khecara</s> (aerial movement).
a mercury pool is situated. || 122 ||
At its northeastern side, from the <s>Chelikā</s> cave,
Entering there facing north, for three <s>dhanuṣ</s> (bow-lengths),
mouse-shaped stones are found; one should collect them. || 123 ||
Grind one of them with buttermilk and drink — one will fall unconscious.
In a moment one rises as a <s>Siddha</s>; one lives for three days of <s>Brahmā</s>. || 124 ||
He himself becomes one who transmutes all metals by mere touch.
Having fasted for a day and night before the deity, one attains perfection. || 125 ||
South of the deity <s>Kapoteśvara</s> are two deities.
Between them, digging to waist-depth — stones resembling <s>gorocanā</s> (cow-bezoar). || 126 ||
Collecting those stones, grind with honey and ghee.
By drinking that, a mortal gains a lifespan of one <s>kalpa</s> — no doubt. || 127 ||
To the northwest of the deity <s>Kapoteśvara</s>, digging one arm's length,
stones resembling pigeons are found — they are touch-transmuters. || 128 ||
One should collect one after performing worship of the deity.
To the northeast of the deity <s>Mallikārjuna</s> is the <s>Bhṛgupātana</s> (Precipice of Bhṛgu). || 129 ||
Near it there is a spring; from it one should collect clay.
Mix it with <s>pañcagavya</s> (five cow-products) and smelt with <s>khadira</s> (Acacia) charcoals. || 130 ||
Metal the color of blue lotus falls out; then quench it
with honey and ghee while very hot — seven times, again and again. || 131 ||
Hold that ball in the mouth — one becomes equal to <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
From <s>Bhṛgupātana</s>, to the east, at a distance of just over one <s>krośa</s>, is <s>Pāṭaka</s>. || 132 ||
Before it is the mountain called <s>Acchatailā</s>, well-known by name.
On its western side is a cave entrance; within it, five desert stretches. || 133 ||

children.text: gate tu dṛśyate kuṇḍaṃ raso lākṣārasaprabhaḥ |
children.translated_text: After traversing them, a spring is seen — a mercury liquid with the luster of lac-juice.
Collecting it in a gourd vessel, it becomes a transmuter at one-ten-millionth proportion. || 134 ||
East of the deity <s>Mallikārjuna</s>, world-renowned,
is the rampart of <s>Candragupta</s>; there exists a temple. || 135 ||
To its east stands a <s>caitya</s> (monument); to the east of the <s>caitya</s>, a great rock.

children.text: mudgavarṇā ca sā khyātā sparśavedhakarā tu sā || 136 ||
children.translated_text: It is known to be <s>mudga</s> (mung-bean) colored — it is a touch-transmuter. || 136 ||
A famous elephant-stone (<s>gaja</s>) is there too; one should mount it with concentration.

children.text: tasya pṛṣṭhāttṛṇaṃ grāhyaṃ tatsarvaṃ kanakaṃ bhavet || 137 ||
children.translated_text: From its back, one should collect grass — all of it becomes gold. || 137 ||
On the northern side of the elephant, digging to knee-depth in the earth,
there are stones shaped like <s>jambū</s> (rose-apple) fruits — they are touch-transmuters. || 138 ||
Or digging below the elephant to knee-depth, one obtains
a supreme perfected triangular pill — it transmutes a hundred thousand times. || 139 ||

children.text: śrīśailasya tu vāyavye tīrthaṃ devahradaḥ sthitam |
children.translated_text: To the northwest of <s>Śrīśaila</s> lies the sacred site, the pool of <s>Devahrada</s>.
In that pool are <s>mudga</s>-colored stones — they are touch-transmuters. || 140 ||
There is a <s>liṅga</s> shaped like a tortoise — a supreme touch-transmuter.
On the full moon of <s>Kṛttikā</s> (Pleiades) asterism, having performed worship, one should collect it. || 141 ||
Two <s>gavyūti</s>-s (about 6 km) from there is a place known as <s>Nīlavana</s> (Blue Forest).

children.text: tatra liṅgaṃ nīlavarṇaṃ jalaṃ caiva tu tādṛśam || 142 ||
children.translated_text: There is a blue <s>liṅga</s> there, and water of the same hue. || 142 ||
Stones resembling horse-mangoes and crows are touch-transmuters.
They exist inside the deity's shrine; one should dig and extract from knee-depth. || 143 ||

children.text: śrīśailasya tu nairṛtye nāmnā guṇḍiprabhā sthitā |
children.translated_text: To the southwest of <s>Śrīśaila</s>, the place known as <s>Guṇḍiprabhā</s> is situated.
From its front, one should collect pit-clay of yellow color and fire in sealed heatings. || 144 ||
From it, gold of brilliant form emerges — no doubt.
There too are bees — they yield the same results as before. || 145 ||

children.text: tathā tambīpure nāmni tīrthe ca vipule śubham |
children.translated_text: Likewise, at the sacred site called <s>Tambīpura</s>, spacious and auspicious,
a well-known ever-fruit is found; a wise person should process it as before. || 146 ||
The deity <s>Mahānandeśvara</s> is to the southwest of <s>Śrīśaila</s>.
To its northeastern side, one should go by the royal road. || 147 ||
The deity called <s>Kālavarṇeśvara</s> — at its front is a pool.
In its midst there is a mercury-liquid resembling <s>indragopaka</s> (a red insect/cochineal). || 148 ||
By sprinkling it on heated seven metals, they become gold.
To the northeast of <s>Śrīśaila</s>, the deity <s>Turaleśvara</s> is found. || 149 ||
To its north, the well-known <s>Umāparvata</s> (Mountain of Umā) stands supreme.
On its summit stand beautiful <s>darbha</s> (sacred grass) stalks resembling tridents. || 150 ||

children.text: tasyādhaḥ kaṭimātraṃ tu khātvā nīlāṃ mṛdaṃ haret |
children.translated_text: Below it, digging to waist-depth, one should extract blue clay.
Cook it with wood produced there (<s>akṣaja</s>); assign a portion to the deity. || 151 ||
Assign portions likewise to guests and to the fire (<s>Agni</s>).
Consume a portion oneself — a man lives for ten thousand <s>kalpa</s>-s. || 152 ||
There, the famous <s>Koṭīśvara</s> near <s>Ileśvara</s> —
At its tip, a mere flower-amount becomes capable of touch-transmutation (<s>sparśavedha</s>). || 153 ||
<s>Acaleśa</s> too is there — another touch-transmutation agent.
To the south of <s>Acaleśa</s>, at a distance of one <s>yojana</s>, there is || 154 ||
a deity called <s>Amareśvara</s>; there is an auspicious gold-stone (<s>svarṇaśilā</s>).

children.text: tasya pṛṣṭhe ca gomāṃsaṃ mahāmāṃsaṃ ca vā kṣipet || 155 ||
children.translated_text: On its back, one should place cow's flesh or great flesh (<s>mahāmāṃsa</s>). || 155 ||

children.text: prajvālya badarīkāṣṭhaiḥ prātaḥ svarṇopamā tu sā |
children.translated_text: Having ignited it with <s>badarī</s> (jujube) wood, in the morning it appears like gold.
A cloth-piece saturated with the menstrual blood of women || 156 ||
should be rubbed on that stone; store it in a gourd vessel.
By mere touch of that, iron becomes gold. || 157 ||
At <s>Śrīśaila</s>, here and there, stones are found lying on the ground in lumps.
Their powder, together with <s>Triphalā</s>, one <s>karṣa</s> — one should consume it always. || 158 ||
Within half a month it destroys old age; one lives as long as the moon and stars endure.
To the southwest of the king of mountains, <s>Paṭāhakarṇa Īśvara</s> is situated. || 159 ||
In the northeastern direction of that deity, at twenty-five bow-lengths,
there is a rock two arm-spans high; dig two arm-spans there. || 160 ||
One should collect thirty stones resembling <s>śrāva</s>-capsules.
Having made them fire-colored, sprinkle with <s>Kūṣmāṇḍa</s> (ash-gourd) juices. || 161 ||
From within them, butter-like substance is obtained — give a portion to the deity,
one portion to a guest, and the wise one should consume one portion. || 162 ||
Unconsciousness occurs for a day and night; upon awakening, the man is reborn.
He lives for ten thousand years, a hero free from wrinkles and grey hair. || 163 ||
The second step of that deity is a touch-transmutation agent.

children.text: tasya devasya pārśve tu pāṣāṇāḥ śvetapītakāḥ || 164 ||
children.translated_text: On the sides of that deity, there are white and yellow stones. || 164 ||
All are touch-transmuters — there is no doubt. One should collect even just one.

children.text: tasya devasya pūrve tu kūpaḥ syānnātidūrataḥ || 165 ||
children.translated_text: To the east of that deity, there is a well, not too far away. || 165 ||
Within it are frog-like stones — they are touch-transmuters.
To the north of that deity, the famous <s>Liṅga</s>-mountain stands. || 166 ||
On its northern side, there is an east-flowing river.
On the western bank of the river, there is a <s>liṅga</s> of tawny color. || 167 ||
There, a pool filled with mountain-water is an instant transmuter.
To the south of <s>Maheśa</s>, at a distance of two <s>yojanas</s>, is <s>Caṇḍikā</s>. || 168 ||
She is famous as <s>Piṇḍādevī</s>; from the northwestern corner of her shrine,
there is a well; within it are stones of <s>mudga</s>-color (green/mung-bean color). || 169 ||
And also ones resembling <s>Pathyā</s> (Terminalia chebula) — all are touch-transmuters.
By the touch of all of these, the procedure of transmutation is accomplished. || 170 ||
If the stone is large, grind it smooth; with that, make a crucible.
The eight metals should be poured into its interior. || 171 ||
All of it becomes gold; thus one should do as desired.
If the stone is fine, then wherever the eight metals || 172 ||

children.text: taṃ sarvaṃ nikṣipenmadhye sarvaṃ tatkāñcanaṃ bhavet |
children.translated_text: are in molten state, cast it into their midst — all becomes gold.
To the northwest of <s>Mallikārjuna</s>, the <s>tīrtha</s> (sacred site) called <s>Sarveśvara</s> is situated. || 173 ||
To the south of it, at half a <s>yojana</s> by the water-route,

children.text: gate ḍāṅgarikaṃ tatra dṛśyate tasya mūrdhani || 174 ||
children.translated_text: having gone, a <s>Ḍāṅgarika</s> (a formation/landmark) is seen there, on its summit. || 174 ||
Black <s>Dhātrī</s> (gooseberry) fruits are found; one should eat them —
as many as desired, for seven days — one becomes diamond-bodied. || 175 ||
Freed from wrinkles and grey hair, one lives for three hundred <s>kalpas</s> (aeons).
From there, to the south, the great forest of <s>Kākalerī</s> — || 176 ||
there is a plantain-pillar (<s>stambhakadalī</s>); the practitioner should enter there.
Going half a <s>krośa</s> (about one mile), a mercury-pool (<s>rasakuṇḍaka</s>) is visible. || 177 ||
Having collected it in a gourd vessel, the mercury becomes a <s>koṭi</s>-transmuter (capable of transmuting ten million-fold).
In that forest, there is a peacock made of blue stone. || 178 ||
At the tip of its beak is a pool, twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> deep, of blue color.

children.text: tanmadhye śuṣkavaṃśaṃ tu kṣiptvā syānnūtanaḥ kṣaṇāt || 179 ||
children.translated_text: Placing a dried bamboo in it — it becomes fresh instantly. || 179 ||

children.text: dine patraṃ phalaṃ puṣpaṃ jāyate tasya nānyathā |
children.translated_text: Within a day, leaves, fruit, and flowers appear on it — not otherwise.
Place one <s>prastha</s> (measure) of mercury there and draw out an equal amount of water. || 180 ||
Drink it in a quantity equal to honey; one instantly becomes unconscious.
Within a <s>muhūrta</s> (48 minutes), one attains sovereignty and lives for a thousand <s>yugas</s> (ages). || 181 ||
On the southeastern side of the mountain, there is <s>Guṭikāsiddha Keśvara</s>.
In front of it, one should dig the earth to a depth of five arm-spans. || 182 ||
There are stones shaped like jujube berries — they grant the power of sky-travel.
Collect even just one and keep it in the mouth — one who wishes to travel the skies. || 183 ||
At <s>Śrīśaila</s>, the procedure for all the yogas described is stated:
Having first performed <s>mantra-nyāsa</s> (ritual placement of mantras), one should then chant one <s>lakṣa</s> (hundred thousand). || 184 ||
The <s>Aghora</s> mantra — by that, one swiftly attains the respective <s>siddhis</s> (perfections).

children.text: kṣetradevatāmāvāhayet | tatra svapne devatā pratyakṣībhūya varaṃ dadāti |
children.translated_text: One should invoke the presiding deity of the site. Then in a dream, the deity appears in person and grants a boon.
devoted to the worship of <s>Śambhu</s> (Śiva), daily observing the ritual of worship,
the accomplishment of the wealth of <s>Śrī Girisā</s> (the mountain-lord, Śiva) should be done — by those devoted to <s>japa</s> (chanting), well-versed in the sacred tradition;
otherwise,
if done with neglect, alas, it will certainly become fruitless. || 185 ||
Thus by those devoted to mantras, most steadfast, devotees and practitioners,

Thus ends the eighth instruction, named 'The Practice at <s>Śrīparvata</s> (the Sacred Mountain),' in the <s>Rasāyana-khaṇḍa</s> (Elixir Section) of the <s>Rasaratnākara</s> composed by <s>Śrī Nityānātha Siddha</s>, son of <s>Pārvatī</s>.
